en: The Sūtra of the Six-Syllable Great Dhāraṇī Mantra.
The translator’s name is lost; it is now appended to the Liang dynasty records.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Bhagavān was dwelling on Vulture Peak Mountain in the city of Rājagṛha.
In the middle [of the assembly], together with a great community of five hundred bhikṣus.
At that time, the Elder Ānanda...
At that time, having been seized by the sorcery of a Caṇḍālī woman, the Elder Ānanda addressed the Buddha,
saying: "World-Honored One,
I am now being forcibly taken away by another."
"Bhagavān, Sugata, I have now been forcibly taken away by another.
Then the Bhagavān said to the Elder Ānanda:
"Come here, Ānanda; do not be afraid."
Ānanda, you should receive and uphold this six-syllable Great Dhāraṇī mantra.
For the sake of bringing benefit, security, peace, and auspiciousness to the practice of the fourfold assembly, I shall now speak the mantra: [Mantra follows]
Sīha, Heṭhi, Tiṭhila, Daṇḍa, Anaka, Chada, Lepamchada, Lekharāchi, Kheyole, Sāti, Bhāti, Yajñabhāti, Tijabhāti, Piṇḍolabhāti. Ānanda, this is the mantra.
It can cause undigested food to be digested immediately;
it can eliminate diseases such as vomiting and diarrhea;
and it can eliminate wind-related disorders.
It can extinguish all febrile diseases, cold-natured diseases,
and miscellaneous ailments; it can destroy all malevolent incantations and sorcery,
and it can eliminate the raising of corpse-spirits.
It can extinguish all forms of sorcery and malevolent charms.
Ānanda, if there are those who know the name and lineage of this divine mantra,
they shall have no fear of royal calamities.
They do not fear the perils of enemies, nor do they fear the perils of bandits;
they do not fear the perils of fire, nor do they fear the perils of water.
Whether in cities, towns, villages, or even in the wilderness, they have no fear whatsoever.
Nor will others seek out his faults, for there will be no faults to be spoken of.
Even if he consumes poisonous medicine, the poison cannot harm him; it will instead be transformed into benefit.
Ānanda, these six syllables of the Great Dhāraṇī Mantra were spoken by seven Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
It was also spoken by Brahmā, the Lord of Sahā;
it was spoken by Śakra Devendra and the Four Great Heavenly Kings.
All of them likewise rejoice in its destruction of all incantations and its subduing of reanimated corpses.
All malevolent images, sorcery, and hexes shall be utterly destroyed and eradicated.
Upon hearing what the Buddha had spoken, the Elder Ānanda rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
*The Sutra of the Six-Syllable Great Dhāraṇī Mantra*.
